measure: r(tail retained in training, RMSE gain)

verdict: DOES NOT GENERALISE AS A PREDICTOR: pooled out-of-sample RMSE gain is -0.05% against a growth-optimum-proxy baseline, and the cytoplasmic control does no worse (+0.11%). It lowers error in 3 of 4 folds, and the pooled figure is decided by the one fold it fails - Pseudomonadota, 49% of the scored genomes and the phylum holding most of the acidophiles, whose removal leaves training with little of the acid-tolerant tail the effect is confined to. Both readings must be carried: the association survives every within-sample test in this paper and does NOT buy out-of-sample accuracy across clades. For a claim about mechanism that is survivable; for any claim about prediction it is fatal, and this paper makes none.
